After the refactor it executes unconditionally on every `SelectMRUTab` call — once per Ctrl+Tab press. `GetWebContentsAt(0)` looks up tab index 0 (not the active tab), which could theoretically return `nullptr` if the strip is empty, causing `FindBrowserWithTab(nullptr)` to be called and the function to bail mid-session. Storing the browser reference on [review thread comment 3089657773 truncated; use get_search_content findText or offset for the full text] - patches/helium/ui/tab-cycling-mru-popup.patch:466 — markwai (resolution state unknown): Ok so I've put the new deferred ActivateTabAt behind tab_cycling_popup_ and now without this new feature enabled, nothing should change - patches/helium/ui/tab-cycling-mru-popup.patch:306 — markwai (resolution state unknown): Yes, it shouldn't be per-keypress. I've moved the lookup back inside the empty() branch and am using `raw_ptr mru_cycle_browser_` to cache the browser on TabStripModel (cycle list already lives there). Also added a nullptr guard ## Appendix ## Full review thread comment 3089657709 **`StopTabCycling` activates a tab unconditionally, double-firing in the non-popup path** When the popup feature is disabled (the default), `UpdateTabCyclingSelection` already calls `ActivateTabAt` on every keypress. `StopTabCycling` then reads `pending_index = model->GetPendingMRUTabIndex()` (the same `mru_cycle_list_[0]` just activated) and calls `ActivateTabAt` a second time. The original `StopTabCycling` never called `ActivateTabAt` at all. The deferred activation is only needed when the popup was shown; in the fallback path it is redundant and fires tab-change events on an already-active tab. Suggested shape for the fix (plain C++, adapt to patch format): ```cpp void BrowserView::StopTabCycling() { TabStripModel* model = browser()->tab_strip_model(); tab_cycling_event_handler_.reset(); if (tab_cycling_popup_) { const int pending_index = tab_cycling_popup_->GetSelectedTabIndex(); tab_cycling_popup_->GetWidget()->Close(); tab_cycling_popup_ = nullptr; if (pending_index >= 0 && pending_index < model->count()) { model->ActivateTabAt( pending_index, TabStripUserGestureDetails( TabStripUserGestureDetails::GestureType::kOther)); } } model->StopMRUCycling(); } ``` This activates the selected tab only when the popup was actually shown (deferred mode) and skips the extra call when cycling happened directly. ## Full review thread comment 3089657773 **Browser lookup now runs on every keypress instead of only on session start** `chrome::FindBrowserWithTab(GetWebContentsAt(0))` was previously guarded by `if (mru_cycle_list_.empty())`, so it ran only once per cycling session. After the refactor it executes unconditionally on every `SelectMRUTab` call — once per Ctrl+Tab press. `GetWebContentsAt(0)` looks up tab index 0 (not the active tab), which could theoretically return `nullptr` if the strip is empty, causing `FindBrowserWithTab(nullptr)` to be called and the function to bail mid-session. Storing the browser reference on session start (inside the `mru_cycle_list_.empty()` branch) and passing it down, or caching it in `BrowserView`, would restore the original semantics. ## Escalation commands - Full view: `gh pr view 1376 --repo imputnet/helium` - Complete diff: `gh pr diff 1376 --repo imputnet/helium` - Stored full document: use `get_search_content` with `offset` or `findText`.

#1378 [FR]: Ctrl+N/P keybinds for navigation in Tab Search

- type: issue
- state: CLOSED (COMPLETED)

## Body
### Description

Allow navigating between tabs with ctrl+n and ctrl+p keybindings.

### Who's implementing?

- [x] I'm willing to implement this feature myself (not this month though)

### The problem

Tab Search (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A) is a really handy feature that makes switching between the tabs easy, especially when you have a lot open.

Right now you can only use arrow keys to change the selection. Here is why Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P should work too:
- Most of other UI elements in chrome already support ctrl+n / ctrl + p. Implementing this would fix the inconsistency and align browser behavior with user expectations.
- <60% keyboards where arrow keys require you to press some combo

### Possible solutions

Implement a patch allowing users to navigate between tabs with ctrl+n and ctrl+p inside of "Tab Search" box

### Additional context

- It's possible that it's not relevant on platforms other than mac
- It's possible that I'm the only one who is using this chrome feature
- This is related to #100 as this keyboard shortcut is widely used in vim
